claims.claim: The two source-stated bounds imply total update time Õ(min{n²,m^(4/3)}). This meets Õ(n√m) when m≤n^(6/5) and when m≥n²/log^{O(1)}n; over all m it is within an Õ(n^(1/4)) factor of the target.
claims.evidence: The source states soft-O(n²) and soft-O(m^(4/3)) bounds. Dividing the sparse bound by n√m gives m^(5/6)/n, which is at most one exactly when m≤n^(6/5). Dividing the dense bound by n√m gives n/√m, which is polylogarithmic when m≥n²/log^C n for a constant C. Writing m=n^a, the available bounds cross at a=3/2. The ratio exponent is 5a/6−1 before that point and 1−a/2 afterward; these functions respectively increase and decrease, and both equal 1/4 at a=3/2. Thus the worst polynomial gap on the simple-graph range is n^(1/4), up to polylogarithms.
claims.witness: The extremal density is m=n^(3/2), where both available bounds are n² while n√m=n^(7/4), giving ratio n^(1/4).
claims.search_method: Recomputed every exponent and threshold symbolically with exact Fraction arithmetic and checked the two monotonic pieces; no floating-point decisions were used.

claims.claim: Corrected balanced-cut lemma: for every order-violating insertion u→v into a DAG, either v already reaches u, so the insertion closes a cycle, or one can find equally sized sets B,F and a cut c such that F consists of the descendants of v at or left of c, B consists of the ancestors of u right of c, the stable order (L\F),B,F,(R\B) is topological after the insertion, and all |B||F| ordered pairs in B×F become newly reachable.
claims.evidence: Use reflexive reachability and set D={x:v reaches x} and A={x:x reaches u}. If D∩A is nonempty, concatenating the two paths proves that v reaches u, and adding u→v closes a cycle. Otherwise D and A are disjoint. For a cut swept from immediately before v to immediately after u, h(c)=|D∩L|−|A∩R| starts negative, ends positive, and changes only by zero or one because no vertex lies in both sets. Hence h(c)=0 at a cut between v and u, where both sets are nonempty. Let F=D∩L and B=A∩R. In the proposed stable reorder, the only potentially reversed old-edge classes are F→(L\F), (R\B)→B, and F→B. The first two contradict descendant or ancestor closure, and the third would imply an old v-to-u path. The new edge is forward because u∈B and v∈F. Finally every b∈B reaches every f∈F through b→…→u→v→…→f, whereas previously f preceded b in a topological order, so b could not reach f. This proves every asserted case and quantifier.
claims.witness: A zero of h(c)=|D∩L|−|A∩R| supplies the required nonempty equally sized sets F=D∩L and B=A∩R; disjointness D∩A=∅ is the key certificate excluding every problematic edge class.
claims.search_method: Proved the sweep and edge-class invariants directly, then exhaustively enumerated all 33,866 DAGs respecting a fixed order on two through six vertices and all 502,170 backward insertions. The checker found 325,405 cycle cases, 176,765 non-cycle cases, and validated all 214,503 balanced cuts, including topological reordering and fresh B×F reachability.

claims.claim: The balanced-cut construction gives an explicit combinatorial algorithm with total time Õ(m+n√m+A), where A is the total number of adjacency entries scanned from selected forward vertices and selected backward vertices. Consequently it attains Õ(n√m) whenever A=Õ(n√m), including sequences in which every selected forward vertex has polylogarithmic out-degree and every selected backward vertex has polylogarithmic in-degree at its expansion time.
claims.evidence: A forward min-heap enumerates descendants of v in increasing current topological order, while a backward max-heap enumerates ancestors of u in decreasing order. Pairing pops until the next frontiers cross produces equally many selected vertices and a cut realizing exactly the sets in claim 1; if v reaches u, the two discovered regions must intersect before crossing along a v-to-u path. Heap insertions other than the two roots are charged to scanned adjacency entries in A, selected-vertex heap and sequence-tree work is Õ(q_i), and ordinary insertions, initialization, and edge storage total Õ(m). For every non-cycle violating update, its q_i² pairs in B_i×F_i are newly reachable. Monotone reachability makes these products disjoint across updates, so Σq_i²≤n(n−1). With at most m such updates, Cauchy–Schwarz gives Σq_i≤√(mΣq_i²)=O(n√m). A terminal cycle search contributes at most Õ(n+A), yielding Õ(m+n√m+A). Under the directional-degree hypothesis, A is at most a polylogarithmic factor times 2Σq_i plus at most n terminal-search vertices. Thus A=Õ(n√m); and for distinct simple edges m≤n² implies m≤n√m. The algorithm uses only adjacency lists, heaps, reachability searches, and a balanced order tree, so it is combinatorial.
claims.witness: The amortization certificate is the disjoint family of newly reachable products B_i×F_i, giving Σq_i²≤n(n−1) and hence Σq_i=O(n√m); all uncharged adjacency work is isolated explicitly in A.
claims.search_method: Checked the search, stopping rule, cycle detection, exact cut realization, reordering, fresh-pair property, and scan-to-heap accounting by exhaustive integer-bitset simulation on all 502,170 fixed-order DAG insertion cases through six vertices. All 325,405 cycle cases and 176,765 cut cases were classified correctly; 1,262,028 scanned entries were accounted for without floating point.

claims.claim: Full adjacency-list rescanning cannot be charged automatically to the balanced-search vertex bound: there is a DAG sequence with n=2r+2 and m=4r in which every violating update has q=1 and creates exactly one new reachability pair, yet rescanning the selected forward list costs r².
claims.evidence: Take the order v,u₁,…,u_r,z,w₁,…,w_r and the 3r initial edges v→w_j, z→w_j, and u_i→z. Insert u_i→v for i=1,…,r. Before update i the maintained order is u₁,…,u_(i−1),v,u_i,…,u_r,z,w₁,…,w_r. The cut immediately after v has F={v} and B={u_i}, so q=1. Before the insertion u_i already reaches z and every w_j, while v reaches only the w_j; after insertion, the only new proper reachable pair is therefore (u_i,v). The graph remains acyclic. Vertex v retains exactly r outgoing adjacency entries and is the selected forward root in every one of the r violating updates, so full-list expansion scans r entries r times. There are n=2r+2 vertices and 3r+r=4r edges, exactly as claimed.
claims.witness: For every integer r≥1, use edges {v→w_j,z→w_j:1≤j≤r}∪{u_i→z,u_i→v:1≤i≤r}, inserting the u_i→v edges last in increasing i. This gives r² repeated scans and only the r new pairs (u_i,v).
claims.search_method: Derived the family parametrically and exactly simulated r=1 through 64 with integer transitive closures, checking 2,080 violating updates, every q value, every newly reachable-pair set, every maintained topological order, edge counts, and scan totals.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an unconditional combinatorial incremental topological-sort algorithm with total update time Õ(n√m) for arbitrary insertion sequences. The draft does not establish that result: claim 0 only compares the two coarser source-stated bounds, while claim 2 proves Õ(m+n√m+A) and reaches the target only under the additional condition A=Õ(n√m). Claim 3 concretely shows why the reachability-pair charge alone cannot bound A under unrestricted degrees. These are correct and material structural and conditional advances, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is warranted, but the arbitrary-degree intermediate-density case remains open within the draft. The final writeup explicitly says that the result is partial and that the exact target remains unresolved; therefore claimed_resolution PARTIAL is ACCURATE and is not a headline overclaim.
